subject: TAN function
notes: PB253 LANDED 2026-09-05: RenderFloat now tests the ARITHMETIC MODE before the RECEIVER SHAPE, so the standard-mode SDIDI arm is reachable from every reference context. PRIOR (PARTIAL): the receiver-less/float test ran first and unconditionally, so under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (and 2002's plain STANDARD, which NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal also selects) the SDIDI arm was UNREACHABLE for every receiver-less or float-receiver reference and the raw binary64 escaped. SPEC BASIS, mechanically re-checked here and not inherited: cite.py --check 15.4.1 "contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect" -> OK; cite.py --check 8.8.1.5.1 "Standard-decimal arithmetic is a method of evaluating an arithmetic expression, an arithmetic statement, the SUM clause, and certain integer and numeric functions as specified in 15.4.1" -> OK, which settles that the FUNCTION itself is evaluated under the mode and not merely its use as an operand; cite.py --check 15.4.1 "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined unless otherwise specified in the function definition" -> OK, the exemption that covers the VALUE (the binary64 approximation) and never the CONTAINER. MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER on the worktree's own cobol.exe, with A = 1.570796326794896619231321691639 and TINY = 1E-20: DISPLAY FUNCTION SIN(TINY) printed 1E-20 (CobolFloat.Display's binary64 E-notation) and now prints 0.00000000000000000001 (the SDIDI's item-92 text); MOVE FUNCTION TAN(A) landed 16331239353195368.96 while COMPUTE r = FUNCTION TAN(A) landed 16331239353195370.00 for the SAME call, and both now land 16331239353195370.00 — the divergence 15.4.1 forbids outright ("the returned value is the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element so long as the value and order of the arguments, the collating sequence, and the locale are unchanged"); MOVE FUNCTION RANDOM(7) and COMPUTE r = FUNCTION RANDOM(7) returned 0.3832204692918902784 and 0.38322046929189024 and now agree. SWEEP: the mechanism is the ORDER, and the fix is at the ONE place all of it renders, so the whole residue moves together — ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, COS, SIN, TAN, LOG, LOG10, RANDOM, i.e. every catalog row with Float: true that RenderNum's standard-mode arm has not already claimed (E / PI / EXP / EXP10 by name; SQRT / FACTORIAL / ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION through RenderDec's alwaysDec list). The sibling receiver-shape-first test at IntrinsicRenderer's NumvalF arm was read and is NOT live: NUMVAL-F is in that same alwaysDec list, so the standard-mode arm claims it before the switch is reached. NumericRenderer.CombineCore, NumericRenderer.Power and NumericRenderer.Landed were each re-read and already test the mode first — RenderFloat was the single outlier from the ordering NUMERIC_DESIGN.md D3 states ("the mode branch runs BEFORE the D16 float branch"), and that doc's prose-family paragraph, which described the container rule as an operand-conversion only, was corrected in the same change set. NATIVE arithmetic is unchanged (re-measured: the binary64 determination of PB13 still holds in every channel). STANDARD-BINARY remains out of scope for the reason the prior adjudication verified: DataBinder rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOL0806, so no function renders under it. The three goldens FAIL against the pre-fix compiler (measured by restoring the pre-fix IntrinsicRenderer.cs, rebuilding and running them) and pass after, so they are evidence rather than decoration. What the prior adjudication established and this landing re-confirms: Math.Tan takes radians per 15.89.1, the argument conversion handles a negative PICTURE-P scale, the empty Codomain column is correct because the tangent is unbounded, and the native quantizer path has no saturation defect. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.TwoPi.cs#ReduceTwoPi (ReduceTwoPi (mod-2pi reduction from 2pi up) was replaced by ReduceQuarterTurns, the quadrant-and-residue reduction that also covers arguments near every multiple of pi/2 (kb/Work PB1041); the new site is on the row)
